newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges Japan not to incite islands incidents.
newsitem.headline: China urges Japan not to incite islands incidents.

text.p: China on Tuesday urged Japan not to provoke new incidents in a row over a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea.
"We hope the Japanese government could adopt truly effective measures and not provoke new incidents," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.

Hong Kong and Taiwan organisers of a high seas challenge to Tokyo's claim over the islands, known as the Diaoyus in Chinese and in Japanese as the Senkakus, returned on Tuesday after being blocked from landing on the group by Japanese coastguards.

Spokesman Shen sidestepped a question on whether Beijing would help Hong Kong and Taiwan activists seek compensation from Tokyo after they fell overboard during attempts to break past the Japanese coastguard cordon around the uninhabited group.

He reiterated Beijing's stance that the Diaoyus were Chinese territory and blamed Tokyo for raising tensions by allowing Japanese right-wing groups to land on the potentially resource-rich archipelago.
"The responsibility lies totally with the Japanese side," Shen said, adding that Japan should prevent further landings on the group by right-wing activists.
